channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: India Gold price today: Gold falls, according to FXStreet data
item.description: Gold prices fell in India on Tuesday, according to data compiled by FXStreet.

item.title: AUD/JPY Price Forecast: Sticks to gains above 112.00 as bulls await 50% Fibo. breakout
item.description: The AUD/JPY cross attracts fresh buyers following a modest Asian session dip to the 111.80 area on Tuesday and turns positive for the seventh consecutive day. Spot prices, however, remain below last week's swing high and currently trade around the 112.15-112.20 region, up nearly 0.15% for the day.

item.title: Swiss Franc gains as US Dollar declines on increased risk appetite
item.description: USD/CHF loses ground for the fourth consecutive day, trading around 0.8200 during Asian hours on Tuesday.

item.title: Gold struggles to lure buyers amid hawkish Fed counters sliding US bond yields
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) attracts some sellers following a modest Asian session uptick on Tuesday and slides below $4,350 in the last hour, though the downside seems limited. The US Federal Reserve's (Fed) hawkish outlook is seen as a key factor undermining the non-yielding yellow metal.

item.title: Australian Dollar drifts higher above 0.7100 after RBA's Bullock speech
item.description: The AUD/USD pair gains ground to near 0.7120 during the early European trading hours on Tuesday. The Australian Dollar (AUD) strengthens against the US Dollar (USD) following Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) Governor Michele Bullock’s speech.

item.title: RBA’s Bullock: Supply shocks are difficult for monetary policy to deal with
item.description: Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) Governor Michele Bullock said in a statement released during the Asian trading session on Tuesday that supply shocks are difficult for monetary policy to deal with. Bullock added, “Policy needs to deal with second-round effects on inflation.”

item.title: US Dollar Index Price Forecast: Needs a decisive move above 100.56 for fresh upside leg
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) holds onto previous day’s gains on Tuesday, with the US Dollar Index (DXY) trading firmly around 100.40.

item.title: EUR/JPY Price Forecast: Remains above 180.50 amid subdued upside momentum
item.description: EUR/JPY extends its gains for the third consecutive day, trading around 180.60 during Asian hours on Tuesday. Technical analysis of the daily chart shows the currency cross remaining within a descending channel, suggesting a persistent bearish bias.

item.title: RBNZ’s Breman: Higher oil prices point to firmer near-term inflation
item.description: Reserve Bank of New Zealand (RBNZ) Governor Anna Breman said on Tuesday that if higher oil prices persist, they are expected to result in somewhat higher near-term inflation than assumed in the September statement.

item.title: British Pound consolidates vs USD; bearish bias remains amid divergent Fed-BoE outlook
item.description: The GBP/USD pair consolidates above mid-1.3300s during the Asian session on Tuesday and remains within striking distance of its lowest level since July 30, touched last week.

item.title: New Zealand Dollar slips amid gradual RBNZ rate hike outlook, geopolitical tensions
item.description: NZD/USD extends its losing streak for the third consecutive day, trading around 0.5700 during the Asian hours on Tuesday.

item.title: Japanese Yen weakens on BoJ's lack of hawkish guidance, eyes on potential intervention
item.description: The USD/JPY pair gathers strength to around 157.55 during the early trading hours on Tuesday. A lack of explicitly hawkish guidance from the Bank of Japan (BoJ) after the rate hike last week undermines the Japanese Yen (JPY) against the US Dollar (USD).

item.title: WTI rises to near $92.50 despite Middle East diplomacy, resuming flows
item.description: West Texas Intermediate (WTI) oil price halts its four-day losing streak, trading around $92.30 per barrel during the Asian hours on Tuesday. However, crude oil prices may face further challenges amid easing supply concerns in the Middle East and growing diplomatic efforts to end the US-Iran war.

item.title: Canadian Dollar hits fresh low since August 5, seems vulnerable vs bullish USD
item.description: The USD/CAD pair touches a fresh high since August 5 during the Asian session on Tuesday, though it lacks follow-through buying and remains below mid-1.4000s.

item.title: PBOC sets USD/CNY reference rate at 6.7459 vs. 6.7487 previous
item.description: The People’s Bank of China (PBOC) sets the USD/CNY central rate for the trading session ahead on Tuesday at 6.7459 compared to the previous day's fix of 6.7487 and 6.6989 Reuters estimate.

item.title: US Treasury Secretary Bessent says all Iranian airlines to shut down worldwide by September 23
item.description: US Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said that Iranian airlines could effectively be shut out of international travel from September 23, as the United States threatens foreign companies with secondary sanctions if they continue servicing the country’s carriers, Aljazeera news agency reported.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: XAG/USD sticks to gains near mid-$66.00s; 23.6% Fibo. holds the key
item.description: Silver (XAG/USD) attracts fresh buyers following the previous day's two-way price moves and trades around the $66.40-$66.45 region during the Asian session on Tuesday, up nearly 0.50% for the day.

item.title: Euro edges higher above 1.1450 despite German political risks, hawkish Fed rhetoric
item.description: The EUR/USD pair trades with mild gains near 1.1470 during the early Asian trading hours on Tuesday. Middle East diplomacy hopes provide some support to the riskier assets such as the Euro (EUR) against the US Dollar (USD). Traders await the Fedspeak later on Tuesday for fresh impetus.

item.title: Donald Trump administration plans $5 billion Middle East reconstruction fund for Iran war
item.description: US President Donald Trump administration ‌has proposed investing $5 billion in a new fund to help rebuild critical infrastructure across the Middle East damaged in the war with Iran and reduce their reliance on the Strait of Hormuz to ‌transport oil and gas, the Wall Street Journal reported on Monda

item.title: RBA’s Hunter backs more hikes as inflation risks entrench
item.description: The Reserve Bank of Australia (RBA) Assistant Governor Sarah Hunter confirmed the need for further rate hikes this year, to keep inflation in check. This has increased the chances for a rate increase at the September 29 meeting.

item.title: Yemeni forces says Houthis drone, fighters targeted
item.description: Yemeni government forces said that they struck Houthi fighters and supply lines near the Bab al-Mandeb Strait and in al-Bayda governorate and shot down a Houthi drone in southwestern Taiz province, aljazeera news agency reported on Monday.

item.title: ECB’s Lane says energy shock could delay inflation’s return to 2%
item.description: The European Central Bank (ECB) Chief Economist Philip Lane stated that the European economy will expand steadily at a moderate pace if the energy shocks ease, according to Le Temps.

item.title: Australian Dollar holds its nerve as Fed hawks meet RBA hike bets
item.description: The Aussie Dollar holds firm versus the Greenback at the start of the week, hovering near 0.7119 as risk appetite remains positive despite Fed officials turning more hawkish than expected, ahead of the Trump-Xi summit in the US, later this week.

item.title: Iranian President will head to New York for UN meeting
item.description: President Masoud Pezeshkian will lead an Iranian delegation at the United Nations General Assembly in New York on Tuesday, amid renewed hopes for a diplomatic solution to the Middle East conflict, CNBC reported on Monday.

item.title: Gold declines to near $4,350 on rising odds of Fed rate hike
item.description: Gold price (XAU/USD) declines to near $4,365, snapping the two-day winning streak during the early Asian session on Tuesday. The precious metal loses ground on the prospect of further monetary tightening by the US Federal Reserve (Fed). Traders will keep an eye on the Fedspeak later on Tuesday.

item.title: The British Pound slips again as bets on an October Fed hike build
item.description: GBP/USD has stalled at 1.3400 in each of the last three sessions, and it trades just under that level again on Monday. The Dollar is up against most major currencies, so this is more a Dollar move than a Pound one.

item.title: The Japanese Yen keeps sliding after the Bank of Japan's split vote
item.description: Japan's markets are shut from Monday to Wednesday for national holidays, which is when a government that wants to move its currency gets the most for its money. USD/JPY is higher for a fifth session in six and is trading just below 157.50.

item.title: NZD/USD Price Forecast: Bears lean on 0.5700 as RSI sinks
item.description: The New Zealand Dollar extends its losses for the second straight trading session, down 0.13% after last week’s Fed rate hike and a hawkish tilt within the board, which was reinforced by speeches of Fed officials on Monday. The NZD/USD trades at 0.5717.

item.title: Silver Price Forecast: 100-day SMA caps bulls as range tightens
item.description: Silver price advance stalled at the 100-day Simple Moving Average (SMA) of $66.39 and is set to end Monday’s session with losses of 0.39% as the Greenback rises following last week’s Fed decision. The XAG/USD trades at $66.03 after reaching a high of $67.05.

item.title: Fed’s Collins eyes another hike as energy risks linger
item.description: On Monday, Boston Federal Reserve (Fed) President Susan Collins said the resumption of hostilities in the Middle East was a key reason for supporting the increase in the Fed funds rate last week.
